findings.asked: Complete a tree diagram and find a combined probability.
findings.wentWrong: Diagrams were decent but the outcome labels were often missing; in the calculation most added the branch probabilities instead of multiplying.

findings.asked: Tree diagram for two groups, then a probability.
findings.wentWrong: Branch ends carried raw numbers (45, 50, 30) instead of fractions; labels were missing; the wrong totals were used as denominators; fractions were added rather than multiplied.
findings.rule: Each branch carries a probability out of its own group's total.

findings.asked: Probability of two independent events combining in a given way.
findings.wentWrong: Many added; of those who multiplied, some counted only (1,4) and (2,3), missing the reversed orders.
findings.rule: List every ordered way the event can happen, multiply along each, then add across.

findings.asked: Complete a tree diagram and find a combined probability.
findings.wentWrong: Probabilities were placed on the wrong branches, labels omitted, and 0.3 + 0.1 = 0.4 appeared instead of the product.
findings.rule: Label every branch with its outcome and its probability.

findings.asked: Tree diagram for two rolls of a dice; probability of no sixes.
findings.wentWrong: Labels were missing; some changed the fractions on the second roll; few multiplied 5/6-type fractions correctly, and an answer over 1 went unquestioned.
findings.rule: Independent events keep the same probabilities on the second set of branches.

ruleToRemember: Label every branch (outcome and probability); multiply along, add across; include every order that fits the event; a result above 1 means something is wrong.
aStarSignal: Un-prompted use of 1 minus P(none) and both orders for a mixed outcome, with the tree fully labelled.
